title: A general, rapid method for creating productive crops from wild plants

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a repeatable way to turn diverse, suitable wild plants into useful crops on a substantially shorter development path than conventional domestication. It would begin with plants that already possess valuable adaptations to their environments and combine the traits needed for cultivation: useful yield, harvestability, product quality, reliable reproduction and workable agricultural management. Retaining the original adaptation is part of the objective.

Conceptual synthesis: the central capability is predicting and producing a viable combination of traits across species. Editing a few known domestication genes can contribute to that process, but does not by itself demonstrate that the resulting plant can function as a crop. A general method would connect genetic changes to whole-plant performance, propagation, field management and the requirements of the intended food or oilseed product.

significance.text: Conditional significance: a reliable general method could broaden agriculture’s plant repertoire and let crop development begin with useful adaptations already present in wild species. Its revolutionary contribution would be to make the creation of new crops more predictable and repeatable, giving breeders more starting points for agricultural environments and uses that existing crops serve poorly.

Conditional downstream possibilities include more diverse crop portfolios and new food or oilseed options suited to particular growing conditions. These benefits depend on retaining the relevant adaptation while achieving acceptable productivity, quality and management requirements. Competitive yields, practical adoption and wider food-system benefits would require evidence for each resulting crop; expanding the number of cultivable species alone would not establish those outcomes.

Interpretive limit: rapid domestication should not be understood as making any wild plant into a valuable crop on demand. The intended generality concerns a method that transfers across diverse suitable species. Biological constraints and the requirements of different products and farming systems would still limit which plants are useful candidates.

missing_breakthrough.text: The proposed missing capability is reliable prediction and assembly of the full crop trait package across diverse wild plants while preserving useful adaptations. The supplied evidence does not establish how close research is to this capability or verify its present absence across the entire field. It nevertheless defines a coherent research objective beyond isolated domestication edits.

Engineering synthesis: a workable method would need to identify which traits limit cultivation in each species, determine genetic changes that improve them, and introduce and combine those changes without undermining other necessary functions. Yield, harvestability, quality, reproduction and management must work together. An improvement in one trait therefore needs evaluation in the resulting plant and production system, rather than being treated as sufficient evidence of successful domestication.

Engineering synthesis: transferability also requires a practical route from genetic intervention to fertile, stable planting material in each target species. The method must preserve the intended adaptation through trait combination and propagation, and establish that it remains useful under field conditions. These are proposed barriers implied by the objective; the supplied scientific artifact does not document their severity, solutions or failure rates across species.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies a reported pennycress example: Barsanti Gautam, Brice A. Jarvis, Maliheh Esfahanian and colleagues, “Creating a new oilseed crop, pennycress, by combining key domestication traits using CRISPR genome editing,” attributed to Nature Plants on 22 January 2026, with DOI 10.1038/s41477-025-02202-7. The research describes combined domestication traits, improved oilseed characteristics and reduced weediness. These are reported findings from the supplied research, rather than findings verified from scientific text in the retained source.

According to the supplied review, the retained PubMed artifact contains only a cookie-access notice and provides no article identity, abstract, methods, results or publication details. The earlier description of an abstract-only assessment therefore overstates the scientific material available for verification. The claimed publisher-opening attempt is also not documented in the retained evidence. These access limitations leave the bibliographic details and reported traits unverified here; they do not show that the study or its findings are false.

Interpretive synthesis: if the reported pennycress findings are confirmed, they would illustrate combining crop-relevant traits in an individual species. They would not alone establish predictable crop creation across unrelated plant families, a general development-time advantage, stable seed systems or competitive field and food-system performance. The supplied material supports no verified quantitative estimates for those outcomes and does not establish the maturity of the pennycress result.

Coverage limitation: no bounded search record was supplied to assess developments through 1 November 2026. This record therefore cannot establish comprehensive current coverage or determine whether later work changes the assessment. The limitation concerns the available evidence and search history, rather than an inference that no further achievements exist.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independently create multiple useful food or oilseed crops from several unrelated wild plant families using a repeatable development method. Select sufficiently different starting plants to test transferability, and define the number and diversity of families before evaluation. Success across that set would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested scope, rather than literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed timing criterion: demonstrate a substantially shorter development path against explicit, relevant conventional domestication or crop-development comparisons. Define the starting point, endpoint and included stages in advance, including the work needed to obtain stable planting material and useful field performance. The supplied inputs provide no established numerical threshold for “rapid” or “substantially shorter.”
completion_criteria.label: Proposed timing criterion

completion_criteria.text: Proposed performance criterion: show stable reproduction and seed systems, useful yield, harvestability, product quality and workable management in replicated field and food-system trials. Compare performance with relevant alternatives for the intended use and environment, and demonstrate that the adaptation motivating selection of the wild species survives domestication and remains beneficial. Define “competitive” using explicit crop-specific measures rather than assuming a single yield benchmark fits every application.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed performance criterion

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundary criterion: have independent teams reproduce the method in additional target species, document development effort and failures, and identify conditions under which the method succeeds or fails. Evidence should distinguish producing an edited plant, producing a stable crop population and establishing a practically useful crop. These are proposed evaluation requirements, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and boundary criterion

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: AGR-01, cereal crops supplied predominantly by biological nitrogen fixation, and AGR-02, a transferable carbon-concentrating system for C3 staple crops, concern particular physiological capabilities. AGR-07 concerns creating viable crops from wild starting species. Either physiological capability could complement a new crop, but successful domestication would not establish either one.

Roster-based synthesis: AGR-03, reliable clonal seed reproduction across major hybrid crops, overlaps with the need for dependable reproduction and propagation. AGR-07 requires a stable seed system appropriate to the resulting crop, without requiring clonal seed reproduction. AGR-04, high-yield perennial versions of the major grain-crop portfolio, overlaps where a wild perennial provides a promising starting point; its target remains perennial versions of major grains, while AGR-07 addresses a broader crop-creation method.

Roster-based synthesis: AGR-05, productive staple farming with seawater and a closed salt balance, could intersect with domestication of plants selected for relevant environmental adaptations. Retaining a plant adaptation would not by itself demonstrate productive seawater farming or close a farming system’s salt balance. AGR-06, rapidly programmable, durable crop immunity, could improve a newly domesticated crop, but durable immunity and general crop creation remain separate capabilities.

Roster-based synthesis: AGR-08, economically accessible, end-to-end autonomous field farming, concerns farm operations. Crop architecture and harvestability developed under AGR-07 could affect compatibility with automated equipment, while neither innovation establishes the other. AGR-09, food crops that reliably build durable, additional soil carbon, could overlap with the selection of useful wild-plant traits; a new crop would still require separate evidence of durable, additional carbon storage.

unresolved_issues: Scientific text is needed to verify the pennycress article’s identity, publication details, combined traits, seed composition, reduced weediness and demonstrated experimental scope.
The supplied evidence does not establish the present breadth or limitations of de novo domestication across species, or whether another result already meets part of the proposed capability.
No bounded search record establishes coverage through 1 November 2026.
The proposed evaluation still needs explicit species and family selection, timing endpoints, comparison baselines, performance thresholds, trial scope and seed-system stability requirements.
Retention of useful adaptations while combining the complete crop trait package remains an objective whose feasibility and reliability cannot be assessed from the retained artifact.
